text.text: A fast, clear proposal wins the booking. Aim to send one within a working day.
The inquiry call
Date, venue, guest count, budget range and service style.
Dietary needs and any cultural or religious requirements.
Kitchen access at the venue and load-in time.
The proposal
Choose dishes from the Menu and check cost per head.
Set the price per head and add staffing, rentals and travel.
State the deposit, the balance date and the cancellation terms.
Send it and set the event to Proposal sent.
Booking
When the contract is signed and the deposit received, move the event to Booked and record the deposit.
Seven days out
Final headcount and dietary list confirmed
Prep items created for every dish
Purchasing list sent to suppliers
Prep days
Work the Prepping this week view each morning.
Cook the longest-lasting items first; assemble delicate items last.
Label every container with the event, dish, date and allergens.
Packing
Pack against the prep list, not memory.
Pack hot and cold items separately, and keep a temperature log.
Press Pack it for each item as it goes in the van.
A forgotten sauce is a small thing until it is the one thing the client remembers.
At the kitchen
Load the van using the loading list and confirm the count with the driver.
Check the staff list and phone numbers.
On site
Meet the on-site contact and confirm the timeline.
Set up the station and check power, water and holding.
Brief the staff on dietary tags and service order.
Photograph the setup for the portfolio, with permission.
After service
Count rentals, clear waste and leave the space cleaner than you found it.
Collect the balance if due and close the event with Close out.
Capturing needs
Ask for dietary needs at booking and again ten days out.
Record allergies as specific as possible; avoid "no nuts" when it should be "tree nuts and peanuts".
On the menu
Food safety
Hold hot food above 135 degrees Fahrenheit and cold food below 41.
Keep a thermometer and a log on every job.
When in doubt, throw it out.
